doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Pay, health and the Gibson guitar
title: Pay in the early years with Gray, Dorsey and Peterson
summary: Ellis recalls $175 a week with Dorsey, a raise with Oscar, and touring Europe with Jazz at the Philharmonic in good hotels.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: In the meantime tell us about what it was like to be a musician in some of the earlier years and kind of what the pay was like.

In the earlier years? Well I was with Glen Grey, you probably don’t even remember that name but that was an orchestra, and they played pretty well. And then when I went with Jimmy I made more and this is back in the ‘40s, you know, the early ‘40s. And I finally got to making, now this will seem ridiculous, $175 a week. But back at that time that was big money you know. And then I joined Oscar and my price went up some. But I’m just amazed, and when we’d travel with Oscar in Jazz at the Philharmonic in Europe, Norman had us booked at the very best hotels. And we could afford it on the money we made. Of course now that’s a different ball game. I don’t know if we’d be able to stay there or not.
